problemStatement.formal: Let $f\in \mathbb{C}[z]$ be monic of degree $n$ with all roots in the unit disk. Let E = {z : |f(z)| ≤ 1}. What is the shortest path in E joining z=0 to |z|=1?
problemStatement.plain: What is the worst-case shortest path in the sublevel set of a monic polynomial with roots in the unit disk?
whyMatters: Connects polynomial geometry to path length

proven: For f(z) = z^n, sublevel set = closed unit disk
Degree 0: sublevel set = all of ℂ
Degree 1: sublevel set = disk of radius 1 centered at root
open: Main conjecture: worst-case path length → ∞ with n
Growth rate of worst-case path length
Optimal bound as function of degree n
knownResults.goal: Formalize setup and prove basic properties; main conjecture requires deep complex analysis

currentState.focus: Survey: formalize definitions and basic properties
blockers: Main conjecture needs arc length theory not in Mathlib
Clunie-Netanyahu existence proof requires topology of polynomial sublevel sets
currentState.nextAction: Gallery integration or further structural theorems if complex analysis APIs mature

knowledge.progressSummary: SURVEY COMPLETED: 214-line formalization with 14 proved theorems, 0 sorries, 5 axioms. Defined UnitRootedPoly, sublevel set, proved 0 ∈ E, characterized f(z)=z^n case, degree 0 and 1 cases.
insights: The problem is fundamentally about complex analysis/topology - hard to formalize deeply
The trivial case f(z) = z^n gives E = unit disk, path length 1
When roots cluster, E develops thin necks forcing longer paths
E is a lemniscate - a level set of |f|
The key difficulty is formalizing arc length and path connectivity in Lean
mathlibGaps: No arc length / path length computation for curves in ℂ
Limited topology of polynomial sublevel sets
No Clunie-Netanyahu type results in Mathlib
nextSteps: Could add IsClosed proof for sublevelSet if continuous_abs API works
Could formalize more about degree 2 case with specific root configurations
